title: Attosecond delay metrology beyond the photon coherence time with spectrally resolved Hong-Ou-Mandel interferometry
authors: Yingwen Zhang, Kyle Jordan, Duncan England, Vincenzo Tamma, Ebrahim Karimi, Benjamin Sussman
abstract: Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interferometry enables delay estimation at the quantum precision limit but is traditionally constrained to path differences within the coherence time of the interfering photons. Here, we demonstrate single-measurement path-delay sensing at the measurement Cramer-Rao bound using spectrally resolved HOM interference, thereby removing the conventional dynamic-range limitation imposed by the photon coherence window, with no scanning required for calibration. By extracting delay information from the spectral interference fringes of spectrally entangled photon pairs, we retain near-optimal sensitivity over an operational range exceeding the photon coherence time by over two orders of magnitude. Using one million detected photon pairs, we achieve a time-delay precision of 20 attosecond (6 nm), while real-time operation (at 1 Hz) yields 330 attosecond (100 nm) precision. Because the estimator relies on fringe periodicity rather than absolute coincidence rates, the method is intrinsically robust to photon losses and variations in interference visibility, eliminating the need for recalibration. As a practical demonstration, we measure the thickness of a 300 um transmissive target with nanometer-scale precision. These results mark a significant step towards deploying quantum-limited measurements in real-world sensing applications using HOM interferometry.
summary: The authors present a method to perform high-precision path-delay measurements using spectrally resolved Hong-Ou-Mandel interferometry. By analyzing the periodicity of spectral interference fringes, they overcome the limitation imposed by photon coherence time, achieving attosecond precision over vastly extended ranges. This technique is robust and demonstrated its utility in real-world nanometer-scale sensing applications.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is overcoming the conventional dynamic range limitation of Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interferometry for path-delay sensing, which is traditionally restricted by the coherence time of the interfering photons.
main_result: By analyzing the periodicity of spectral interference fringes rather than just the dip depth, the method achieves near-optimal sensitivity over ranges exceeding the photon coherence time by over two orders of magnitude.
method: Delay information is extracted from the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) applied to the spectral interference fringes generated by spectrally entangled photon pairs. This approach is robust because it relies on fringe periodicity rather than absolute coincidence rates.
model_or_system: The experiment uses a Hong-Ou-Mandel interferometer setup employing spectrally entangled photon pairs generated via Spontaneous Parametric Down-Conversion (SPDC). The measurement utilizes custom two-photon spectrometers based on time-tagging event cameras to resolve the spectral correlations.
key_observables: Spectral interference fringe periodicity, measured path delay ($\Delta t$ or $\Delta z$), and measurement precision ($	ext{SD}t$ or $	ext{SD}_z$).
important_parameters: Attosecond time-delay precision (20 as); operational range exceeding coherence time by $>10^2$; spectral resolution ($\xi$) and photon bandwidth ($4\sigma^2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis involves modeling the measurement using approximations for the large-delay regime, where sensitivity is governed by the periodicity of the joint spectral amplitude fringes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the conceptual setup (Figure 1), show spectral interference fringes persisting at large delays (Figure 2), plot achieved precision against theoretical limits (CRB) over extended ranges (Figure 3), and demonstrate practical thickness measurements using path delay tracking (Figure 4).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the limitation of standard HOM sensing to introducing spectral resolution as a solution. It details the theoretical framework based on joint spectral amplitudes, presents experimental results showing enhanced range and precision, and concludes with practical demonstrations like thickness measurement.
why_interesting: This work represents a significant advancement in quantum metrology by extending the operational regime of an established quantum optical technique (HOM interferometry) far beyond its fundamental coherence limit using spectral domain analysis.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Conceptual setup for spectrally resolved HOM interferometry. Broadband spectrally entangled photon pairs are generated in a nonlinear crystal pumped by a 405 nm CW laser. One photon propagates through a channel or object that introduces an optical path delay to be monitored or measured. The two photons are then recombined at a 50:50 beamsplitter (BS), where they undergo HOM interference. The output photons are directed to custom spectrometers based on time-tagging event cameras. In each spectrometer, the photons are spectrally dispersed by a diffraction grating and imaged onto the camera.
